lines.text: Between now and 2028, about thirty-eight thousand people will move into brand-new public estates in Hong Kong's Northern Metropolis.
They'll get the keys to a new flat. What they won't get is neighbours.
Nearly half of the working adults here commute more than an hour each way. So in the daytime, these estates belong to older residents and children.
By 2031, more than one in four people in North District will be over sixty-five. Yet the whole district has just one elderly centre, and the new transport links are still being built.
Around half of older people in Hong Kong already feel lonely or isolated. Moving somewhere new, where nobody knows your name, only makes it harder.
Visiting teams can't be there every day. Step counters count steps, not friends.
But people here already walk. Every day, along the same paths, past the same faces.
So we built StreetWalk: an app that turns those daily walks into real neighbours.
Setup takes a minute. Pick your building, choose an avatar, with a walking cane or a wheelchair if you like, and hear, out loud, exactly who can see what.
Then just walk. StreetWalk notices when you start walking and records it automatically. No buttons. It even learns where home is, from where your phone spends the night.

Your neighbourhood appears as a paper-cut model of the streets around your home. The circle board shows people who regularly walk nearby. But until you've met, they only see a nickname and a cartoon avatar.
There's no friend search, and no invite link. The only way to connect is to meet in person. Bump phones, and you're neighbours. Ultra-wideband detects the bump, and a QR code covers older phones.
When a neighbour heads out, you hear it. Mrs Chan just left, probably near the pavilion. A landmark, never a map pin. And it grows right out of the Dynamic Island.

To meet up, just say it. Walk with Mrs Chan tomorrow at three. AI picks a spot you both pass, with seats and shade, and tells you why. Anything that affects someone else is read back before it's sent.
On the day, finding each other is easy. Within fifty metres, your phone buzzes, and a big arrow points the way. No map to read.
On hot days, StreetWalk checks the Observatory forecast against building shade, and suggests a cooler time to head out.
Say, it's too sunny here, and that feedback is pinned to the nearest landmark. Each month, anonymous summaries, only where ten or more residents agree, go to social workers and estate management.
Everything works by voice, in Cantonese or Mandarin, with large text, and a big button behind every voice command.
Privacy is built in. Your exact location never leaves your phone. Our server only sees landmark names. Strangers can never see where you are, and your home is always hidden.
And this isn't a mock-up. StreetWalk has a live backend shared between phones, real location tracking, ultra-wideband pairing, and more than two hundred automated tests.
StreetWalk supports good health and inclusive communities: Sustainable Development Goals three and eleven.
Because in a new estate, every walk is a chance to meet a neighbour.
